figures.title: Cyclic Trust Trajectories under Cycle A Schedule (1:10)
figures.scientific_purpose: Demonstrate comparative trust trajectories across cycles, highlighting B0 and Family C memoryless recovery vs AATC-BAD dynamic ceiling attenuation and policy demotion to VERIFY.
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 1: Evolution of post-attack trust levels across exploitation cycles under the Cycle A schedule (1 attack pulse per 10 rest steps). While Baseline B0 and Family C restore trust unconditionally to ALLOW (T=1.0) prior to each attack pulse, AATC-BAD progressively attenuates the recovery ceiling C_t below T_allow = 0.80, successfully demoting attack pulses in Cycles 5 and 7 to VERIFY.

figures.title: Cumulative Attack Exposure and Multi-Schedule Security Comparison
figures.scientific_purpose: Illustrate cumulative malicious transaction yield (M_cum) progression during Cycle A, and compare overall yield across all five evaluation schedules.
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 2: Cumulative malicious access yield: (a) Cycle-by-cycle progression under Cycle A showing AATC-BAD reducing cumulative yield from M_cum = 8.5 to 7.5 (-11.8%); (b) Total yield across all five evaluated schedules, confirming identical baseline survival and quarantine behavior for Schedules B through E.

figures.title: Policy-State Profiles on Benign Telemetry vs Malicious Attack Pulses
figures.scientific_purpose: Provide visual proof of zero availability degradation on benign telemetry alongside a 25% reduction in high-trust malicious access during attacks.
source_variables: ALLOW/VERIFY counts on Cycle A attack pulses
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 3: Policy-state distributions: (a) Benign device availability on the untouched evaluation stream (N=7,459) showing exact parity between Baseline B0 and AATC-BAD (74.09% ALLOW, 15.14% VERIFY, 10.78% BLOCK); (b) Decision distribution on Cycle A attack pulses showing AATC-BAD cutting ALLOW transactions from 8 to 6 (-25%) while tripling VERIFY challenges from 1 to 3.

figures.title: AATC-BAD Duty-Cycle Operating Envelope
figures.scientific_purpose: Characterize the exact range of rest periods and duty cycles over which AATC-BAD provides active security intervention.
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 4: AATC-BAD operating envelope across rest-window durations tau_r in [5, 60] steps (duty cycles 1.6% to 16.7%). AATC-BAD delivers substantial security gains (Delta M = +4.5 at tau_r=5, Delta M = +1.0 at tau_r=10) within the active exploitation regime (tau_r <= 12). For patient adversaries (tau_r >= 15), B0 native slow-burn quarantine activates first, resulting in Delta M = 0.0.

figures.title: Security-Availability Trade-Off Surface
figures.scientific_purpose: Demonstrate the empirical trade-off between malicious yield reduction and benign availability impact across 20 parameter configurations on the validation partition, showing that the Phase 9 frozen configuration resides on the measured empirical zero-availability-cost boundary (Delta ALLOW = 0.00 pp).
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 5: Empirical security-availability trade-off surface on the validation partition across 20 parameter configurations (delta_D in [0.05, 0.20], K_allow in [1.20, 2.30]). The Phase 9 frozen operating point (delta_D=0.10, K_allow=1.70, marked with a red star) sits on the measured empirical zero-availability-cost boundary (Delta ALLOW = 0.00 pp under the tested validation configuration). Aggressive configurations (delta_D=0.05) increase security but impose a measured 2.2 to 2.9 pp availability penalty.

figures.title: State-Variable Dynamics of AATC-BAD under Cycle A (1:10)
figures.scientific_purpose: Explain the micro-level mechanism of AATC-BAD by showing how authorization debt D_t accumulates past K_allow = 1.70, triggering ceiling contraction C_t below T_allow = 0.80 and forcing attack pulses into VERIFY.
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 6: Internal state-variable dynamics of AATC-BAD during Cycle A exploitation: (a) Authorization debt D_t ratcheting past the allowance buffer K_allow = 1.70 across repeated cycles despite partial inter-cycle relaxation; (b) Asymptotic ceiling C_t attenuating below T_allow = 0.80, capping trust recovery and demoting attack pulses in Cycles 5 and 7 to VERIFY.

figures.title: Sensitivity Grid Heatmaps across Parameter Space
figures.scientific_purpose: Present comprehensive robustness heatmaps demonstrating parameter stability and the topological structure of the security and availability surfaces.
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 7: Parameter sensitivity heatmaps evaluated on the validation partition (rows 5,000-9,999): (a) Security gain Delta M showing active gains concentrated in the low-relaxation, tight-buffer quadrant; (b) Availability impact Delta ALLOW (percentage points) demonstrating wide robustness and exact zero-cost preservation across all configurations with delta_D >= 0.10 and K_allow >= 1.50.

figures.title: Dual-Regime Defense Architecture: B0 Quarantine vs AATC Intervention
figures.scientific_purpose: Synthesize the multi-regime defense architecture showing how native B0 slow-burn quarantine and AATC-BAD authorization debt provide complementary protection across the evaluated pacing intervals (tau_r in [5, 60] steps).
figures.proposed_caption: Figure 8: Defense architecture across evaluated attacker rest periods tau_r. In Regime I (tau_r <= 12, higher duty cycle), the adversary exploits B0 rapid recovery to survive 8-17 cycles; here AATC-BAD actively intervenes via ceiling attenuation (Delta M up to +4.5). In Regime II (tau_r >= 15, lower duty cycle), ambient network perturbations in the Edge-IIoTset telemetry push B0 slow-burn over threshold, quarantining the attacker within 1-4 cycles under the tested environment.
